With that caveat, calculating year-over-year growth within each company's own fiscal calendar:

- Walmart: Revenue grew from $605,881 million in FY2023 to $642,637 million in FY2024 [DOC-2], a growth rate of approximately 6.07% (($642,637 − $605,881) / $605,881).
- Oracle: Revenue grew from $49,954 million in FY2023 to $52,961 million in FY2024 [DOC-1], a growth rate of approximately 6.02% (($52,961 − $49,954) / $49,954).

Both companies posted very similar year-over-year revenue growth rates for their respective fiscal 2024 periods — Walmart at roughly 6.1% and Oracle at roughly 6.0% — despite Walmart's revenue base being more than 12 times larger than Oracle's. The growth rates are nearly identical in percentage terms, though the periods are not perfectly time-aligned due to the differing fiscal year end dates.

ANSWER: Walmart's FY2024 revenue grew ~6.07% (from $605,881M to $642,637M) while Oracle's FY2024 revenue grew ~6.02% (from $49,954M to $52,961M) — nearly identical growth rates, though the two companies' fiscal years cover different 12-month periods (Walmart ends Jan 31, 2024; Oracle ends May 31, 2024), so the comparison is not perfectly time-aligned.
